newsitem.title: USA: U.S. raises dumping duties on Mexican cement.
newsitem.headline: U.S. raises dumping duties on Mexican cement.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Commerce on Friday raised dumping duties on Mexican cement imported between 1993 and 1995, a department spokeswoman said.

The spokeswoman said the department's International Trade Administration had issued the final dumping margins for two reviews of periods covering August, 1993 to July, 1994 and August, 1994 to July, 1995.
For the first period, it imposed a duty of 109.85 percent and for the second one it decided a 103.8 percent duty.
The previous dumping margin in the cement dispute, which began in 1988 at the instigation of U,S. companies, was 62 percent.
According to the spokeswoman, Mexican cement companies would have to pay duties retroactively for shipments imported to the United States during those periods.
The Mexican government, which had learned about the increases earlier, said it would complain to the United States over the Department of Commerce's decision.
